tag_types.definition: physical quantity calculated, plotted, fitted, or numerically compared
tag_types.requirement: represents something that can take a calculated, measured, fitted, plotted, or numerically compared value, distribution, or functional dependence

tag_types.definition: quality or adjective-like modifier of another tag
tag_types.requirement: represents a non-quantitative quality or adjective-like modifier of another tag; a numerical observable or claim-validity range does not qualify

tag_types.definition: theory, computational method, model, formula, code, or experimental method used to obtain results
tag_types.requirement: represents a reusable theory, procedure, model framework, formula, code, or experimental technique used to obtain or analyze results; a specific parameter set, dataset, or model instance does not qualify

tag_types.definition: research object class or physical system
tag_types.requirement: represents a class or category of research objects or physical systems; one specifically named object, nucleus, isotope, or dataset does not qualify

tag_types.definition: specific named object, nucleus, isotope, author, model instance, or dataset
tag_types.requirement: represents one specifically named or uniquely identified object, nucleus, isotope, author, model instance, parameter set, or dataset; a general class or reusable method does not qualify

tag_types.definition: parameter range, density region, nucleus range, or other condition under which a claim holds
tag_types.requirement: represents a range, regime, selection criterion, or constraint that limits when, where, or to which objects a claim applies; the research object or its intrinsic property does not qualify

tag_types.definition: observable physical phenomenon or event discussed in the paper
tag_types.requirement: represents a physical process, event, or observable behavior; its numerical descriptor, governing method, or applicability condition does not qualify

claim_types.definition: defines a concept, quantity, or method
claim_types.requirement: explicitly states the essential meaning, defining relation, defining equation, or identification criterion of a concept, quantity, or method; merely stating its use, effect, or behavior does not qualify

claim_types.definition: introduces established context for a concept
claim_types.requirement: explicitly states an established role, relationship, scope, or characteristic of a concept needed to introduce the paper's research context; merely mentioning or using the concept, or reporting a current-work result, does not qualify
explicitly states an unresolved problem, scientific need, importance, or reason for pursuing the current objective; merely stating the work performed or objective does not qualify
explicitly states something the current analysis treats as true, fixed, approximated, constrained, or neglected; a reported condition or result does not qualify

claim_types.definition: describes how a result is obtained
claim_types.requirement: explicitly states how the current work uses a procedure, model, formula, data source, or computational or experimental step to obtain results
explicitly reports an outcome, value, trend, dependence, or observed behavior produced by the current work
explicitly states a difference, similarity, agreement, disagreement, ordering, or other relative relation between at least two methods, models, calculations, measurements, datasets, or prior results

claim_types.definition: states the paper's explicit new contribution, novelty, or main advance
claim_types.requirement: explicitly presents a contribution, improvement, capability, or advance of the current work as new or novel; novelty must not be inferred from an ordinary result
